text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Dutch painter, JAN VERMEER, who painted realistic scenes of serene and harmonious domestic life, was born in 1632.
French inventor BENOIT FOURNEYRON, who developed the water turbine, was born in 1802.
Chinese leader of the Nationalist People's Party, CHIANG KAI-SHEK, who was exiled from China after being ousted by the Communists, was born in 1887.
Australian snooker player EDDIE CHARLTON, who was National champion 15 times and World champion in 1976, was born in 1929.
British drummer with the 'Babys', TONY BROCK, was born in 1953. He was also a session musician with ROD STEWART, EDDIE MONEY, RANDY VANWARMER and JIMMY BARNES.
UK guitarist and songwriter with the Scottish group 'Texas' ALISTAIR McERLAINE was born in 1968.
** EVENTS **
1517 : MARTIN LUTHER posted his 95 theses, an attack on
various ecclesiastical abuses, on the door of Wittenberg Palace, marking the beginning of the Protestant Reformation in Germany.
1888 : A Scottish veterinary surgeon developed a new type

of tyre. JOHN BOYD DUNLOP patented the new tyre, which consisted of an all-rubber inner tube covered by canvas with a rubber tread, on this day. His invention came from attempts to reduce the vibrations from the solid rubber wheels on his son's tricycle.
1926 : Escape artist and conjuror HARRY HOUDINI died of

peritonitis. The Hungarian-born magician was 52. His stage act earned him an international reputation. He escaped from straitjackets, handcuffs, prison cells and locked, weighted and submerged containers.
1932 : In the United States FRANKLIN ROOSEVELT detailed

his New Deal. The package included the introduction of a five-day week and federal aid for the unemployed. The following month ROOSEVELT was swept to power in a landslide victory defeating the Republican's HERBERT HOOVER.
1933 : The United States research ship Atlantis returned
to port with evidence of life in the deepest parts of the oceans.
1935 : In Britain the school leaving age was raised from
1940 : The Battle of Britain officially declared at an
end after the loss of 915 Royal Air Force aircraft and 1733 Luftwaffe planes.
1955 : Princess MARGARET ended three weeks of world
speculation and announced that she had decided not to marry Group Captain PETER TOWNSEND.
1958 : The first internal heart pacemaker was implanted
by Dr AKE SENNING in Stockholm.
1961 : Russia's de-Stalinisation programme reached a
climax when his body was removed from the mausoleum in Red Square and re-buried.
1963 : "Beatlemania" was at its peak in Britain.

Screaming fans clogged the streets around the London Palladium when the Liverpool group starred in a television programme. The fans caused traffic jams, one which delayed the prime minister. Next month the "Fab Four" topped the bill at the Royal Command Variety Performance.
1971 : An IRA bomb exploded at the top of London's Post
Office Tower.
1984 : The Indian prime minister Mrs INDIRA GANDHI was

shot dead by her bodyguards. The two men, both Sikhs, riddled Mrs GANDHI with bullets as she walked in the garden of her New Delhi home. Mrs GANDHI had ignored repeated warnings about the potential danger of keeping Sikh bodyguards. She was 67.
1987 : Two young people were said to have committed
double suicide near Canberra. They were found beheaded and strapped in the front seat of their car with their heads mysteriously placed in the back.
1994 : Former New South Wales Police Minister TERRY
GRIFFITHS resigned from the Liberal Party, after he was dis-endorsed by the party following allegations of sexual harrassment were made against him.
